main_body: A bare, dead gothic tree: a thick trunk rising from a flat base plinth and splitting into several bare branches. The drawing is a pure side view of an organic form with no horizontal top surface.
top_band: none (the column at x=24 runs dark brown outline, mid brown, dark brown and mid brown bands for the branch, then the trunk body L=35 for rows 33-62; no lighter horizontal top surface)
evidence: This is an organic tree, a bare trunk with branches. It has no horizontal surface that should read as a top, and the form is a trunk silhouette with no separate top and front. Trees are normally judged on silhouette and shading, and there is no flat-top contract violation like a rim or a lid. The tonal bands in the scan are branch cylinders and bark shading, not a top band. The trunk base is a flat dark plinth. The kind is organic and matches. Because the trunk is a vertical form with no top surface, a strict reading of the contract gives no top band, but the object is an organic tree rather than a box-like piece, so I do not fail on the 3/4 rule alone.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 7 distinct colours and a median of 5 colours per tile, against 108-109 per tile and 427-567 colours for the references. Its 93% near-neutral dark edge pixels (#16110f) show a near-black outline, while the references' outlines are tinted (0% neutral). Its ramp has only 3-4 brown steps (#16110f, #33281f, #594736 and a few others). The trunk and branches are banded in simple stripes with little bark grain, leaf clumping or texture dots. It is a bare tree that will naturally have less foliage, but even so the bark is much shallower than the leafy references' shading, so it looks thinner and more sticker-like beside them.
